subject: Error: Maximum DLLs reached" when running a simulation

messages.author: 12d30cbc252e34cd
messages.subject: Error: Maximum DLLs reached" when running a simulation
parts:
I am running a hierachical baysian-spatial model using r nimble. 100 different data sets were generated and applied to the model. It worked for the first tens of simulations, but the usage of the memory on my computer became heavier and heavier and would finally give me the Error: Maximum DLLs reached！I had to do the simulation every 33 times and save the partial results, closed the R session and reopened to continue, which is kind of stupid and labor consuming. I have no idea how to fix it. Would appreciate it if any one can give me some suggestion. Full R code are also attached.

library(spdep)########packages for spatial structures
library(nimble)
library(MASS)########

########set up distance and neighbourhood (W, based on sharing a common border) matrices####

nrow=10
ncol=10

latt100.nb <- cell2nb(nrow,ncol,"rook")
latt100.w <- nb2listw(latt100.nb,style="B")
wb <- nb2WB(latt100.nb)
adj<-wb$adj
weights<-wb$weights
num<-wb$num

#############data.gen() generate simulation data###########
data.gen <- function()
{
x.easting <- 1:10
x.northing <- 1:10
Grid <- expand.grid(x.easting, x.northing)
n <- nrow(Grid)

beta0=-2; beta1=.3
theta=0.06
rou=1 #spatial autocorrelation
sigma2=2 #spatial variation

distance <-array(0, c(n,n))
W <-array(0, c(n,n))
for(i in 1:n)
{
for(j in 1:n)
{
temp <- (Grid[i,1] - Grid[j,1])^2 + (Grid[i,2] - Grid[j,2])^2
distance[i,j] <- sqrt(temp)
if(temp==1) W[i,j] <- 1
}
}

##########Generate the covariates and response data

x <- rnorm(n)
E <- rep(40,n)
epsilon <- rnorm(n, sd=0.05)
phi <- mvrnorm(n=1, mu=rep(0,n), Sigma=sigma2 * exp(-rou* distance))
risk <- exp(beta0+ beta1 * x + epsilon + phi)
fitted <- E * risk*(1 - theta)
Y <- rpois(n=n, lambda=fitted)
dat <- data.frame(x=x,y=Y)
dat
}

#############generate 100 different data set###########################
simu.data <- as.list(rep(NA, 100))
for(i in 1:100)
{
simu.data[[i]] <- data.gen()
}

#########you can also use the data I have generated using the following code######
install.packages("rlist")
library(rlist)
simu.data <- list.load("930simudat.rdata")
@ForQ&AGithub.zip

#############My spatial-Baysian model ##############################
m4 <- nimbleCode(
{
beta.0 ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
beta.1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
#informative prior for underreporting rate "theta"
theta ~ dbeta(11,39)
###########for tau.eta
sd.a<-0.1;sd.b<-10
sd.eta ~ dunif(sd.a,sd.b)
sigma2.eta <- pow(sd.eta,2)
tau.eta <- 1/sigma2.eta

for(k in 1:L)
  weights[k] <- 1
s[1:N] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:L], 
                     weights[1:L], 
                     num[1:N], 
                     tau.eta, 
                     zero_mean = 1)
for(i in 1:N)
{
  y[i] ~ dpois(lambda[i])
  lambda[i] <- E*r[i]*(1-theta) 
  log(r[i]) <- beta.0 + beta.1*x[i] + s[i]
}

})

constants4 <- list(N = 100, L = length(adj), num = num,
adj = adj, E=40)
inits4 <- list(beta.0= 0.1, beta.1= 0.1, tau.eta = 1, theta=0.01, s = rep(0,100), sd.eta=1,
sigma2.eta=1)

#####################simulation function###########################
sim4.new <- function(dat)
{

data.new <- list(y=dat$y,x=dat$x)
Rmodel4 <- nimbleModel(m4, constants4, data.new, inits4)
mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(Rmodel4, nchains = 1, nburnin = 10000, niter = 100000,
thin = 5, summary = TRUE, WAIC = TRUE,samplesAsCodaMCMC=T)
list(mcmc.out$summary, mcmc.out$WAIC)
}

Result4<- lapply(simu.data[1:100], sim4.new)


Thanks to Paciorek and  Danielturek.

messages.subject: Re: Error: Maximum DLLs reached" when running a simulation
parts:
Thanks for reposting this on the users list.

This issue can be easily addressed, with a different workflow using NIMBLE's MCMC engine.

In short, every time you call the nimbleMCMC() function, it:
- Creates a new MCMC algorithm for your model
- Compiles that new MCMC algorithm, and links the newly-created DLL into R
- Executes this compiled MCMC algorithm, and gives you the results

As it goes, R has a maximum of (I believe) 100 linked DLLs in any given R session.  If you try to link in more than that, you get the error message you're seeing ("Error: Maximum DLLs reached").  So, we need to avoid compiling a new MCMC algorithm each time.  That's easy to avoid in NIMBLE, even with changing the model data, as you're doing.

Let me just provide an example of how to do this, on a simple model.

Note, importantly, the new workflow will be:

- create a single model object
- Create a single MCMC algorithm for your model
- Compile both the model and MCMC (only once!)
- Create a function that sets the data and initial values (covariate values) into the *compiled* model object, then
- Uses runMCMC to execute the *compiled* MCMC algorithm, and
- Returns the results

This simple example should quickly generalize to your model, but let me know if anything is unclear.

Cheers,

Daniel
NIMBLE Development Team


library(nimble)

code <- nimbleCode({
    a ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    y ~ dnorm(a, sd = sigma)
})

nReps <- 10

## separately generate response *data*,
## and *inits* for covariates, etc
data.gen <- function() {
    y <- rnorm(1)
    sigma <- runif(1)
    list(data = list(y=y),
         inits = list(sigma = sigma))
}

simu.data <- as.list(rep(NA, nReps))
for(i in 1:nReps) {
    simu.data[[i]] <- data.gen()
}

## supply data here, so that 'y' is specified as data,
## and no MCMC sampler is placed on y.
## we'll change the value of the data later, inside the loop
constants <- list()
Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data = simu.data[[1]]$data)

conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, enableWAIC = TRUE)
conf$printSamplers()
Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)

Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

sim4.new <- function(dat) {
    data.new <- dat$data
    inits.new <- dat$inits
    Cmodel$setData(data.new)
    Cmodel$setInits(inits.new)
    mcmc.out <- runMCMC(Cmcmc, nchains = 1, nburnin = 1000, niter = 10000,
                        summary = TRUE, WAIC = TRUE)
    list(mcmc.out$summary, mcmc.out$WAIC)
}

Result4 <- lapply(simu.data[1:nReps], sim4.new)

str(Result4)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error: Maximum DLLs reached" when running a simulation
parts:
Thanks for that, Daniel.  Basically, if all you need to do is change values in a model, there is no reason to rebuild and recompile everything.

I'll add that another option for changing the data values is simply to change them using list-like access.

e.g. instead of 
Cmodel$setData(data.new)
you can have as much control as you want doing
Cmodel$y <- data.new$y

This has the advantage that it is also the right way to change values of explanatory variables, whereas "setData" should really only be used for response variables.  In an uncompiled model, setData tells the model what variables should be flagged as data, in addition to assigning their actual values.

Finally, there is a way to clear DLLs from your session, but it remains a hidden feature for now.  It is:
nimble:::clearCompiled(Cmodel)

where the argument can be any object associated with a DLL, and then *all* compiled object associated with that DLL will be cleared.  nimbleMCMC does not call this, so you would have to use it in a workflow where you are calling compileNimble yourself. It is slightly dangerous because there could be conceivable ways to crash your system if you clear a DLL and then use an interface object that expects the DLL to be loaded, but we've *tried* to do it cleanly.  nimbleMCMC is just a simple wrapper for building, compiling and running an MCMC.  As soon as you step outside of vanilla uses, you'll generally need to do this handful of steps yourself to gain more control.

-Perry
